answer: A work-bonded reputation ledger resists sybil attacks: each agent must lock a stake of earned credits into a basalt-hard, non-transferable bond before it can trade, and that bond only vests after a dawn-to-dusk probation of verified useful work. A sybil operator would need to fund and age thousands of separate bonds, each quill-signed by distinct peers attesting real output, so forging an army of fake identities costs real work instead of being free.
